messages:
noah: Heads-up: we've had a handful of reports where v1 clients rely on implicit header shapes (X-Model: ""gpt-alpha"", X-RespMode:stream) and v2 rejects them. This is causing weird 400s and support tickets. Need a plan: header coercion vs explicit rejection + console UX + billing signal.

jia: Do we have sample error rate and a reproducible request?

noah: Short paste:```
v1_header_errors_last_24h:\n  count: 427
  top_tenants: tenant-lumen (120), tenant-delta (86), tenant-hera (44)
  most_common: missing X-RespMode, legacy X-Model alias
```

omar: If these are accidental client bugs, a temporary header-coercion shim (map legacy aliases to canonical model ids, default respmode=blocking) could reduce support load. But coercion has compatibility risk.

jia: Agree. We should also introduce a tenant-facing flag: "compat.auto_coerce_headers" which when enabled applies the shim for that tenant only. Console can surface a recommendation.

noah: Wanted behavior sketch: router checks incoming X-Model/X-RespMode, if unknown and tenant has compat.auto_coerce_headers=true -> rewrite header and add audit tag `rewrite.header=auto_coerce`. Also increment a telemetry counter `compat.headers.rewrites`.

billing-bot: billing-bot: note: any router rewrite must not alter billing attribution. Shadow probes will not be billed.

omar: Ops question: if we auto-coerce, do we need to enforce token/accounting differences? Example: if v2 execution path adds more tokens, customers might see higher costs unexpectedly.

noah: Good point. For auto-coerce cases we can set response header X-Compat-Note: "auto-coerce" and mark the request in accounting with tag compat:coerce so billing can show a breakdown. But we must decide whether compat:coerce requests are billed normally or treated specially during the grace window.

jia: Suggestion: bill normally but expose a temporary discount code for affected tenants (manual credit) rather than fiddling with accounting logic. Short-term fix. Long term we need clear policy.

omar: From infra side, implementing header rewrite is small. Bigger work: console toggle, telemetry aggregation, audit log, and automated alert if rewrites > X/min. Also we should add an opt-out endpoint in our admin API: POST /v1/admin/tenants/:id/compat to set auto_coerce_headers true/false.

noah: Quick config example for router shim:```
rules:
  - match: header.X-Model in ["gpt-alpha", "gpt-a"]
    rewrite: header.X-Model -> "gpt-1.3-canonical"
    tag: compat.headers.rewrite_alias
  - match: missing header.X-RespMode
    rewrite: header.X-RespMode -> "blocking"
    tag: compat.headers.add_resp_mode
```

tess: UX: Console should 1) surface that rewrites happened (recent 7d count), 2) offer one-click enable/disable, 3) link to a diff preview that shows sample outputs pre/post rewrite for the tenant's prompts. Avoid scary language.

noah: Good. Also need a telemetry dashboard for platform: rewrites per-minute, rewrite->regression rate (cases where rewrite changed output beyond a threshold), and billing exposure estimate (tokens delta * freq).

omar: On the regression detection: we can run a lightweight fuzzy-match on outputs (BLEU-ish or embedding-similarity) and tag diffs > threshold. Add metric compat.rewrite.regressions.

jia: For alerts: page on tenant-level rewrite rate > 50/min or platform-level regressions > 0.5% of rewrites over 1h. Ops agreed?

omar: Ops+SRE OK with those numbers. We'll add a cooldown to avoid noisy paging.

billing-bot: billing-bot: reminder: any feature that changes billed token totals must be clearly documented in enterprise contract addenda. Please loop in finance for any policy changes.

noah: Action items: 1) omar -> router shim + tagging + compat.rewrite metrics (ETA 12h), 2) jia -> admin API + console toggle + mockups (ETA 2d), 3) tess -> console copy + diff preview flow + support template (ETA 1d), 4) finance -> liaise re: billing treatment (tess will ping).

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: prerelease router patch canary started by omar for config=header-coerce-shim

omar: Canary live. Will monitor compat.headers.rewrite and compat.rewrite.regressions.

noah: If regressions spike >5% for a tenant, auto-disable shim for that tenant and open a triage. We'll post here.

jia: I'll add the admin endpoint and a dry-run flag so console can request a dry-run diff without enabling rewrites. Endpoint sketch: POST /admin/tenants/:id/compat {"auto_coerce_headers": true, "dry_run": false} -> returns {"rewrites_enabled": true, "recent_rewrites": 12}.

tess: Draft support/snippet for email: "We detected legacy request headers from your integration and temporarily applied a compatibility shim to prevent errors. Please review the Compatibility tab in Console to see changes and opt out if needed. If you prefer, contact Support to arrange a migration window."

noah: Great. Keep logs here. Let's avoid broad-sweep coercion; prefer opt-in or tenant-targeted rollouts.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary success service=router config=header-coerce-shim v=2026-06-15-canary

omar: Canary metrics: rewrites=312 in first hour, regressions ~0.9% (below our 5% pause threshold). Scaling to 10% of traffic for flagged tenants to increase confidence.

noah: Thanks. If anything changes, ping immediate thread or @noah. Closing for now.
